clue.text: Petrarch's muse hasn't left distinctive impression

indicators.note: 'hasn't left' tells us the letter standing for left is missing from the muse's name

parts.note: Laura was the woman the Italian poet Petrarch addressed in his love sonnets

explanation.surface: A remark that the poet's inspiration has not departed, only left a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the usual abbreviation for left, so 'hasn't left' drops it from LAURA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive atmosphere or impression that surrounds a person or place.

clue.text: Insect taken by lizard, last two disappearing in warm island

parts.note: an ant is a common insect

indicators.note: the final pair of letters of the reptile's name vanish, leaving it two letters short

parts.note: the iguana is a large tropical lizard

explanation.surface: A lizard snaps up an insect somewhere hot, its tail end fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' is only a link joining the insect to the shortened lizard; Antigua lies in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island with a warm tropical climate.

clue.text: Healthy again, worried after weeks of debt?

indicators.note: 'of' here is read as made of, with the debt wrapped round the rest

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt

indicators.note: 'after' places the worrying behind the weeks

parts.note: November, abbreviated Nov, is a run of weeks: a month
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried

explanation.surface: Someone recovers, then frets once weeks of debt have passed.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'weeks' as one month is loose, and 'of' as a container signal is unusual. Collins gives renovate as restore health or spirits, so 'Healthy again' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Renovate can mean restore to vigour or health, so a person renovated is restored and well once more.

clue.text: Here one may be resigned to a 0-1 defeat

definitions.text: Here one may be resigned to a 0-1 defeat

parts.words: Here one may be resigned to a 0-1 defeat
parts.note: a player who resigns at chess loses, recorded as 0-1; the clue points to the place where that happens

explanation.surface: A gloomy sports fan accepting a narrow one-nil loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 0-1 looks like a football score, but it is how a chess result is written when Black wins; resigning is how a chess player concedes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess games, and so resignations, take place on the chequered playing surface.

clue.text: Hooker should have sounded fit again

indicators.note: 'sounded' says the word for recovered is said aloud to give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: healed means made well or fit again

explanation.surface: A remark that a prostitute should have seemed recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: The hooker is a rugby forward, who heels the ball back in the scrum, not a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the hooker's job in a scrum is to hook the ball back with the heel.

clue.text: Dunk beer mugs to swill round

indicators.note: swilling liquid round sloshes it about, so the letters of the two words are mixed

explanation.surface: Instructions to plunge beer mugs in water and rinse them about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swill round' reads as washing-up instructions; 'to' is a link and 'swill round' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To dunk something is to push it under liquid, which is to submerge it.

clue.text: Film cheeseboard containing something from East Anglia

indicators.note: 'containing' means the cheese-and-board pair holds the marshland word between its halves

parts.note: Brie is a cheese and a counter is a board, so the word splits into those two
the Fens are the flat marshlands of East Anglia, in eastern England

explanation.surface: A film reviewer's cheese platter holds an East Anglian speciality.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits at 'Film', but the definition is that one word; the film is David Lean's 1945 romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief Encounter is a classic 1945 British film about a chance railway-station romance.

clue.text: Like garden to be irregular

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London

explanation.surface: A garden designed to be untidy and irregular.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew is crooked or out of line, hence irregular.

clue.text: Full of whiskey, coloured, but not maudlin

indicators.note: 'Full of' means the coloured word holds the whiskey inside it

parts.note: dyed means coloured
rye is a whiskey made from rye grain

explanation.surface: Someone full of whiskey and flushed, yet not sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry-eyed means not crying, the opposite of tearfully sentimental.

clue.text: Cover chest and back fully

definitions.meaning: to cover the chest is to get dressed in a top garment
to back fully is to bet everything one has on a single outcome

explanation.definitionFit: Literally, dressing the torso; idiomatically, staking all one's money on a horse or result.

clue.text: Shearing's travelled endlessly over the poles

indicators.note: 'over' means the shortened travel word is laid over and around the poles
'endlessly' cuts the final letter from the travelling word

parts.note: toured means travelled
N and S stand for the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A sheep's fleece-removal has gone round the world from pole to pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter of TOURED; 'over' then wraps that around the poles. The 's in 'Shearing's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaving of part of a monk's head, a kind of shearing.

clue.text: By welcoming danger, start to learn fast

indicators.note: 'welcoming' means the two-letter word takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: taken as written
risk means danger

indicators.note: 'start to' picks out the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone who embraces danger in order to learn quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link word but is the outer piece of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Briskly means quickly, at a fast pace.

clue.text: Make personal betrayal, the sale far too cheap?

definitions.meaning: to reveal one's own secret or feelings unintentionally
a whimsical sense: selling oneself so cheaply it is effectively a free gift

explanation.surface: A traitor sells out personally at a ridiculously low price.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means reveal oneself unwittingly; literally, handing oneself over for nothing.

clue.text: Sound hesitant on worker's Internationale?

indicators.note: 'on' in an across clue places the hesitant sound after the worker

parts.note: an ant is the classic crossword worker; the 's is a link
to hem is to make a hesitant clearing of the throat

explanation.surface: A worker mumbling hesitantly through the socialist song.
explanation.walkthrough: The Internationale is the socialist song, an example of an anthem, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Internationale is the socialist movement's rallying song, an example of a national-style hymn.

clue.text: Was in great doubt before, with plan rejected —— no good

parts.note: ago means before, in the past

indicators.note: 'no good' removes G, the abbreviation for good
'rejected' turns the plan back to front

parts.note: a design is a plan

explanation.surface: Someone was badly torn earlier, the scheme turned down as worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DESIGN into NGISED; 'no good' drops the G, leaving NISED.
explanation.definitionFit: To agonise is to wrestle painfully with a decision, as when deeply unsure.

clue.text: Team extremely sorry to point out I left

indicators.note: 'extremely' takes only the two ends of the word sorry
'I left' means the letter I departs from the pointing word

parts.note: indicate means point out

explanation.surface: Teammates, deeply apologetic, have to admit that the narrator walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives SY from sorry; INDICATE loses its I to give NDICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndicate is a group working together for a common purpose, a team.

clue.text: Familiar piece of music from Copenhagen, say

definitions.meaning: Chambers gives a sense meaning any much-played, familiar musical work
Copenhagen was the Duke of Wellington's charger at Waterloo

explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists a warhorse as any familiar piece of music, and Wellington's mount was literally a horse of war.

clue.text: From base, find way into wood on exercises

indicators.note: 'on' in an across clue sets the wood after the exercises

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: 'into' puts the way inside the wood

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Instructions for a woodland exercise route starting from a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is a link before the definition; 'find' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a column or statue stands.

clue.text: For fun do this on donkey or duck

definitions.text: For fun do this on donkey
definitions.meaning: the children's party game of pinning the tail on a donkey
a species of long-tailed dabbling duck

explanation.surface: A party game played on a donkey, or alternatively on a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is 'pin the tail on the donkey', so the answer splits as PIN TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The pintail is a slender duck named for its long pointed tail feathers.

clue.text: Establish exclusive control of set-piece

definitions.meaning: to monopolise a market by buying up the supply
in football, a kick from the angle of the pitch is a rehearsed set play

explanation.definitionFit: One cornering a market controls it alone; a football corner kick is a set play.

clue.text: Money-raising Joplin festival?

parts.note: Scott Joplin wrote ragtime pieces called rags, so a festival of them is pictured as a week of rags

explanation.surface: A charity fundraiser devoted to the music of Scott Joplin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British student charity fundraising week; Joplin's ragtime pieces are 'rags'.
explanation.definitionFit: British student unions hold a week of charity stunts and collections under this name.

clue.text: Tolerates men in drunken state?

parts.note: tolerates means puts up (with); in a down clue PUTS written upward reads STUP
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword term for soldiers who are not officers, men

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with men in a drunken condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tolerates' is 'puts up', which in a down clue means PUTS written upwards; OR (other ranks) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed near-unconscious state, such as heavy drinking brings on.

clue.text: How sitting should be conducted, anyway

definitions.meaning: a sitting should be done without anyone standing

explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding means nevertheless; split up, it says sitting is done without standing.

clue.text: Chinese rulers accept Welsh accent

indicators.note: 'accept' means the dynasty takes the letter inside

parts.note: the Tang were a Chinese imperial dynasty

explanation.surface: Chinese emperors embrace a Welsh way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal quality of speech, a regional accent.

clue.text: It provides plug with suitable alternative

definitions.text: It provides plug with suitable alternative

parts.note: a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad
apt means suitable
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A device that gives an electrical plug a fitting substitute socket.
explanation.walkthrough: Plug looks electrical, but here it is an ad, a bit of publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor lets a plug fit a different socket, supplying a suitable alternative connection.

clue.text: Title always included in writing

indicators.note: 'included in' puts always inside the writing

parts.note: a page is a sheet of writing
e'er is the poetic form of ever, always

explanation.surface: A noble title that will forever appear in written records.
explanation.definitionFit: A peerage is the rank or title of a peer, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Into truck, began moving fruit

indicators.note: 'Into' puts the rearranged letters inside the truck

parts.note: lorry is the British word for a truck

indicators.note: 'moving' shifts the letters of began about

explanation.surface: Somebody started loading fruit onto a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures fruit being loaded, but 'began moving' is the fodder and its signal, and 'Into' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The loganberry is a cross between a raspberry and a blackberry, a soft fruit.

clue.text: Nibble a quantity of dry stuff

definitions.meaning: to nibble is to take small bites, as birds do
a measure of volume for dry goods such as grain, two gallons

explanation.definitionFit: A bird pecks at food in small bites; a peck is also a dry measure of two gallons.
